server-actions.summary: Server Actions are React Server Functions that Next.js exposes as POST endpoints. Know how they are defined, how their single-roundtrip response works, how the client queues them, and which security checks are yours to write.
points: Define with `'use server'` at the top of a file (all exports) or inline in a Server Component. Client Components cannot define them, only import them or receive them as props.
Invoke from `<form action>`, `formAction` on submit buttons and inputs, event handlers or `useEffect`, ideally inside `startTransition`. The client dispatches actions one at a time.

The response re-renders the current route only if the action calls `updateTag`, `revalidatePath` or `refresh`, mutates cookies, or calls `redirect`. `revalidateTag(tag, 'max')` is stale-while-revalidate and skips that re-render.
`redirect` throws (keep it outside `try`, or use `unstable_rethrow`), defaults to `push` in actions, and sends a 303 for no-JavaScript form posts.

Built-in protections: Origin/Host CSRF check with `allowedOrigins`, a 1 MB body limit, encrypted action IDs (rotated at most every 14 days) with dead-code elimination, and encrypted closure variables (`NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` for multiple instances).
Inside every action: authenticate, authorize the specific resource, validate input with a schema, and return only what the UI needs. Model expected errors as return values for `useActionState`.
traps: Checking auth in the page does not protect the actions it renders; they are reachable by direct POST.
`Object.fromEntries(formData)` includes `$ACTION_` fields and any key the caller adds; never spread it into a database update.
React 19 resets uncontrolled form fields after a form action completes, even when it returns an error, so echo values back as `defaultValue`.
